ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in square $ABCD$, $E$ is a point on side $CD$, and $F$ is a point on the extension of side $BC$, with $CE=CF$. If $\angle BEC=80^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle EFD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
it follows that BC=CD, and $\angle$BCE=$\angle$DCF=90$^\circ$,\\
since CE=CF,\\
it follows that $\triangle$BCE$\cong$$\triangle$DCF, $\angle$CFE=$\angle$CEF=45$^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle$CFD=$\angle$BEC=80$^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle$EFD=$\angle$CFD−$\angle$CFE=80$^\circ$−45$^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is marked as a square, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point E is located on side CD, and point F is located on the extension of BC to the right; BE, EF, and DF are connected in the figure. Since CE is along the vertical side CD, and CF is along the horizontal extension of BC, CE and CF are perpendicular. Then reason: Because ABCD is a square, BC=CD, and ∠BCE=90°, ∠DCF=90°. The problem statement gives CE=CF. Therefore, in △BCE and △DCF, there are BC=CD, CE=CF, and the included angles are both 90°, so △BCE≅△DCF (SAS). Thus the corresponding angles ∠CFD=∠BEC=80°. In addition, in △CEF, CE=CF and CE⊥CF, so △CEF is a right isosceles triangle, hence ∠CFE=45°. From the figure, ray FE is located inside ∠CFD, therefore ∠EFD=∠CFD−∠CFE=80°−45°=35°. Final answer: 35°
